text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

On the back of massive falls in earnings in its domestic building products and construction materials businesses, building materials giant Boral Ltd yesterday reported a 30 per cent fall in net profit to A$205.7 million, compared with A$239.9 million last year. The result forced Boral to reduce its dividend from 21 cents to 18 cents, despite a promise last year to maintain or increase its dividend. Page 1.

Taking advantage of improving notebook sales, Toshiba this week released a A$12,200 machine which is one of the first notebooks to use Intel's 150MHz Pentium processor. Top-of-the-line notebooks have become a status symbol for senior executives and typically stay with their first owners for as little as 18 months. Page 1.

According to Monsanto Inc's crop protection unit president, Arnold Donald, the company has decided to charge Australian farmers A$245-a-hectare - more than twice the price in the US - for its new pest-resistant cotton based on average higher insect infestations here. Page 4.

Goodman Fielder managing director David Hearn yesterday described the company's $28.3 million net profit as a solid performance marked by a significant turnaround in several parts of the business. Analysts said the result was in line with market expectatons and although the first half of this financial year would continue to be affected by wheat prices, the fundamentals for a much stronger performance in the year ahead and beyond were in place. Page 31.

WMC Ltd experienced a 31 per cent increase in after-tax profit following record nickel and copper production and higher uranium prices. Group consolidated profit rose to A$392 million on a 19 per cent rise in revenue to A$2.67 billion, the strong profit result prompting an increase in the annual dividend from 20 cents to 22 cents, although the final payment was lower, dipping from 12 cents to 11 cents. Page 32.

Shares in Lihir Gold and Niugini Mining jumped yesterday as speculation continued about takeover talks between Niugini Mining and US-based miner Battle Mountain Gold. Niugini Mining continued to build on its recent records jumping another 13 cents to the $4 mark with Lihir Gold rising 11 cents to A$2.53. Page 32.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an address to the Economic Society in Melbourne, Reserve Bank deputy governor Graeme Thompson said yesterday that he saw no compelling reasons to radically overhaul the Australian financial system, which appears to be working reasonably well. The Government's Wallis inquiry into the financial sector starts its formal deliberations next week. Page 23.

After yesterday announcing a full-year profit of A$386.2 million, up 20 per cent on the A$351.6 million earned last year, WMC Ltd forecast a year of slow growth, with its offshore projects stalled by political problems and its local production expected to be flat. Page 23.

After reporting disappointing annual profits yesterday, food companies Goodman Fielder Ltd and Arnotts Ltd ARN.AX are hoping to turn around their financial problems with the launch of rationalisation programs. Arnotts announced an 18.3 per cent drop in net proft before abnormals to A$69.2 million and Goodman Fielder reported a 3.5 per cent rise in net profit before abnormals to A$100.7 million. Page 23.

Mayne Nickless Ltd admitted to the Federal Court yesterday that some parcels carried by its Ipec Air Express business were delivered by road transport even though customers may have expected them to be transported by plane. The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission came up with evidence against Ipec by planting altimeters in parcels supposed to fly between Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane. Page 23.

Hazelton Airlines Ltd yesterday announced a net loss of A$2.46 million for 1995-96 after a A$5.2 million writedown in the value of five aircraft. However, company secretary Greg Russell said the New South Wales regional carrier might benefit this year frm the cost-cutting plans of Qantas Airways and Ansett Australia. Page 24.

The worst home building market since the early 1980s contributed to Boral Ltd's net profit slump from A$294 million to A$205 million announced yesterday. The result means Boral will break last year's promise to maintain or increase payouts to shareholders, with a fully franked dividend of 7.5 cents a share to be paid out, down from 10.5 cents last year. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Like rivals CSR, James Hardie and Pioneer, Boral's sales and earnings have been hit hard by the downturn in Australian building, resulting in a 30 per cent dive in net profit after abnormals for the June 30 year to A$206 million, compared with A$294 million previously. Managing director Tony Berg yesterday refused to predict growth in earnings and dividends in the current year. Page 25.

Membership, crowd numbers and television ratings for Sydney Swans games have soared this season, providing the AFL club with a perfect opportunity to tap the market for major long-term sponsorship deals. Sponsorship revenue for the Swans rose 35 per cent this year, with new sponsors joining the club, including the Sydney Harbour Casino and Rebel Sports. Page 25.

Contrary to Treasurer Peter Costello's view that a radical overhaul of Australia's financial system is needed, Reserve Bank deputy governor Graeme Thompson indicated yesterday the bank would suggest to the Wallis financial inquiry that no drastic changes are needed as the current regulatory environment works well and can cope with change. Page 25.

Despite a second-half slump in commodity prices, WMC yesterday posted a 20 per cent increase in June-year equity profit from A$320.8 million to A$386.2 million. WMC offered a final dividend of 11 cents a share, fully franked, taking the full-year payout to 22 cents a share. Page 25.

Australasian operator of the giant cinema screen Imax, Cinema Plus, is to go public to fund its construction plans for eight theatres to be built in Australia and New Zealand over the next five years. Two thirds of the 31 million shares will go to institutional investors and the other third to the retail market at A$1 per share. Page 27.

Company chief executive of food group Goodman Fielder, David Hearn, warned that high wheat and grain charges would continue to have a negative impact on the poultry, milling and baking operations. However the company is confident of a good profit performance for 1996 despite the impact of high raw material charges and intense competition on the supermarket shelves. Page 27.
THE AGE

The Reserve Bank challenged the Federal Treasurer's call for a 'super-regulator' yesterday with Reserve's deputy governor Graeme Thompson saying the proposal to create one 'mega-regulator' was unnecessary and could lead to possible constraints on managed funds. Head of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission Allan Fels said he would recommend to the Wallis committee that restrictions on shareholding and foreign takeovers of banks should be axed if Australia was serious about competing in a global financial services market. Page C1.

WMC weathered the second-half slump on commodity prices led by increases in production to post a 20 per cent increase in June-year equity profit from A$320.8 million to A$386.2 million. Managing director Hugh Morgan said the results were largely in line with sharemarket expectations and he was pleased with the group's achievements in such a challenging year, citing the four deaths at WMC's local and overseas operations as the only area of disappointment. Page C1.

Boral yesterday cut fully franked final dividends from 10.5 cents a share to 7.5 cents after reporting a 45 per cent drop in net profit to A$171 million. Net profit totalled A$205.69 million after abnormal gains of A$34.78 million, compared with a net profit after abnormals in 1994-95 of A$293.88 million. Page C3.

Compared with last year's A$52.8 million loss, Goodman Fielder yesterday announced an A$81 million turnaround to a net profit of A$28.3 million for the year to 30 June. The result prompted chief executive David Hearn to predict an improvement in earnings this year. Page C3.

Announcing a 28 per cent fall in profit to A$273.03 million yesterday, New Zealand-based investment house Brierley Investments failed to reveal any details about its plans for its Coles Myer interests. Chief executive Paul Collins said it was too early a stage in the investment to say whether the company is going to buy more share in Coles or not. Page C3.

Arnotts ARN.AX plans to close its New Zealand operation in Auckland and charge A$33 million as an abnormal item in the earnings for the six months ending 31 January 1997 as part of a strategy to arrest its decline in market share. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
